entry.title: Sam Carlisle Discusses Co-development and Outsourcing in the Game Industry
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com

Co-development differs from traditional outsourcing in how external partners integrate into a studio's workflow. While traditional outsourcing typically operates on a "time and materials" basis for specific assets, co-development involves partners working directly within a studio's engine and version control systems, granting them greater ownership of the production process.

This model enables studios to scale production and absorb economic volatility while protecting core internal teams from layoffs. Successful external collaboration depends heavily on prioritizing transparent communication and personal relationships over technical ability alone.

entry.title: Paranoia-Sans Typeface Automatically Redacts Conspiracy Terms
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion

This typeface uses OpenType ligatures to automatically redact terms associated with conspiracy theories. By replacing keywords like "5G" with a black box graphic, the font simulates the visual appearance of redacted documents.

Developed by Florian Egermann and based on Courier Prime Sans, the project serves as a satirical exploration of the visual aesthetics of conspiracy myths. The open-source typeface aims to mirror the absurdity of the subjects it redacts through its automated functionality.

entry.title: Irish Games Fund Expands with New Funding Strands
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The Irish Game Makers Association (IMIRT) and Screen Ireland Digital Games Portfolio have expanded the Irish Games Fund for 2026, introducing three distinct funding pathways: a Development Fund, a Prototype Fund, and a Release Fund. The currently active Development Fund offers €50,000 to four teams to assist in transitioning validated concepts and prototypes into full production.

Eligible applicants must be registered Irish studios with at least one year of operation, a history of filed accounts, or previously released commercial projects. The fund has implemented strict guidelines regarding generative AI, stating it will not support projects that plan to use machine learning-generated art, audio, or writing in their final commercial releases due to ongoing intellectual property and copyright risks.

entry.title: Bastardica Tool Enables Font Mixing and Transformation
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | bastardica.mitpit.com | hacker news

Bastardica is a web tool for creating customized fonts by mixing, stretching, or squishing source typefaces. It utilizes OpenType's `liga` contextual substitution across all scripts to swap glyphs, allowing users to create "bastard" fonts where characters from a mix-in font replace those in a base font. All font processing is performed locally in the browser via Pyodide and fontTools, ensuring source fonts are never uploaded to a server.

The tool generates standard OpenType files compatible with design software and web browsers. Users can adjust glyph alignment using Y-offset and scale effects, and can minimize glyph collisions when mixing multiple fonts by using prime numbers for character strides. Because mixing fonts produces derivative works, users must verify the licensing of their source fonts for commercial use.

entry.title: Matt Greer Develops Eridin for GBA and PC Using Unified Codebase
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | mattgreer.dev | discussion

Eridin, a fantasy turn-based strategy game, is being developed for both the Nintendo Game Boy Advance (GBA) e-reader and PC to mitigate manufacturing risks. This dual-platform target addresses the difficulty of producing the high-precision dot-strip cards required for reliable e-reader scanning.

The engine uses a single C codebase with an abstraction layer for platform-specific assets, employing DevKitPro and libtonc for GBA and SDL2 for PC. While the PC version maintains the 240x160 GBA resolution, it features subpixel scrolling and uncapped framerates for smoother visual performance.

entry.content:

Versions of Marvel's Wolverine released in certain regions, specifically cited as the Middle East, have reportedly been stripped of LGBTQ+ content. Users have documented instances where references to the marriage between characters Mystique and Tyger—including in-game photographs, audio, and subtitles—were blurred, muted, or replaced with asterisks.

This follows a precedent by Sony and Insomniac Games, who modified Marvel's Spider-Man 2 to remove pride flags and specific character subplots for distribution in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. These changes align with regional laws in those countries regarding the depiction of homosexuality.
